newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN seeks $15 million to avoid famine in Laos.
newsitem.headline: UN seeks $15 million to avoid famine in Laos.

text.p: The World Food Programme (WFP) appealed on Tuesday for nearly $15 million to feed 420,000 people threatened by famine in Laos, some of whom have been reduced to eating lizards and rats to survive.
The funds will be used to import 43,000 tonnes of rice to help rural families in Laos' traditional "rice bowl" region survive until the harvest in six months, a spokeswoman said.
Three typhoons last September caused the heaviest flooding in memory in central and southern Laos, which had been suffering drought, according to the U.N. agency.
Laos' food deficit is 179,000 tonnes out of a total one million tonnes needed to feed its population of four million.
"WFP is launching an appeal for $14.9 million for 420,000 people threatened by famine in Laos," WFP spokeswoman Christiane Berthiaume told a news briefing in Geneva.
"These are the most vulnerable who need urgent aid. The most needy are reduced to begging, rummaging through the garbage, eating lizards and rats to survive," she added.

The Rome-based WFP plans to distribute 400 grams of rice per day to the rural families in the most affected farm provinces of Khammouane, Savannakhet and Champassak, as well as the provinces of Salavana, Attapeu and Sekong, according to Berthiaume.
WFP's Stephen Keller, who left Vientiane on Monday, was in Bangkok on Tuesday to explain the needs to donor countries. Buying rice in Thailand would reduce costs.
Australia has announced it will send 1,300 tonnes of rice, while Canada, Norway and Japan have expressed an interest in making contributions, according to the spokeswoman.
